description: Tell the SurfCAD tab which phase the user's prompt is in. responding (alias typing): you are reading or writing an answer; the chat stays open with bouncing dots. building (alias working): you are creating or editing geometry; the chat collapses and the field shows "Agent is working...". Call set_status { state: "building" } only once you have everything you need and are actually creating or editing geometry. Do not call building to list parts, faces, edges, or transforms, or for status or read_messages. A model-changing tool also enters building if you skip this call. A read never does. set_status is for progress and does not close the task. A partial reply does not leave building; the final reply, Stop, or a disconnect does. No activity for 15 minutes, while responding or building, shows the stall notice and leaves Stop up. The result state is the tab value (responding and typing are typing; building and working are working). Without id it targets the latest prompt. A cancelled id returns { ok: false, error: cancelled }. When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left.

id.description: Optional prompt id this status refers to.

label.description: Optional short text for the tab, for example what you are working on.

state.description: responding: bouncing dots, chat stays open (alias typing). building: you are creating or editing geometry and the field shows Agent is working (alias working). Call building only once you are actually modeling. idle: not responding or building. Idle does not close the task; a closing reply_to_user does.

working.description: Legacy form of state: true is building (working), false is idle. Use state.

name: set_status
